title: Choose the visual world for Royal Valley
question: The roll assigned the Fair Show-Print. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Grand Champion Show-Print
options.lineage: Walla Walla Fair & Frontier Days letterpress posters, blue-ribbon premium books
options.thesis: The trailer billed like the headline act of the valley's season: a letterpress show poster that names it Grand Champion of event restrooms.
options.viewport: Full-bleed royal-blue poster sheet: stacked wood-type 'ROYAL VALLEY' cropped by the edge, wine-to-gold split-fountain rule, the night string-light photo set in like a halftone plate, rosette badge '3 STATIONS · CLIMATE CONTROLLED', two phone numbers as the ticket line, Book button as the admission stub.
options.risk: Fair/rodeo vernacular could read folksy for a black-tie wedding if the ink and type are set cheaply.

raised.raise: Type is set at architectural scale and cropped by the frame, not politely centered.
Every spec (12′ × 8′, 3 stations, 2 hookups) ruled as measured, tabular figures like chalk marks.
Signature interaction: each station door's VACANT/OCCUPIED indicator flips character-by-character.
Center-axis symmetry is the layout law of every poster sheet.

options.label: Estate Wine Label
options.lineage: Walla Walla AVA estate labels and tasting-room menus
options.thesis: The trailer presented like an estate release: 'Station No. 1, 2, 3' set as a vintage label with tasting notes for comfort.
options.viewport: A single tall label centered on deep cabernet: crest, 'Royal Valley — Estate Restroom — Walla Walla', tasting notes listing amenities.
options.risk: The most familiar luxury look in this category and in wine country; it is where most runs land.

options.label: Hand-Bent Neon
options.thesis: The brand as one continuous neon script that lights up when the party goes past dark.
options.viewport: Night photo, dark ground; 'Royal Valley' bends and ignites as one cobalt stroke above the trailer.
options.case: Wedding neon signs are a real trope, so couples identify; loses on clarity since neon says bar, not restroom comfort.
options.risk: Can tip into nightclub and lose daytime corporate bookers.

options.label: Street Typography
options.thesis: Wood-type capitals shouting at architectural scale.
options.case: Same family as the roll but urban NYC, not the valley; loses audience identification and ties on clarity.
options.kept: Architectural-scale type cropped by the frame.

options.label: Split-Flap Board
options.thesis: Event dates and stations as a departures board.
options.case: No real availability data to show; bookers don't identify with transit.
options.risk: Implies live availability that doesn't exist.

options.label: Blacksmith Forge
options.case: No link to events or comfort.
options.kept: Specs ruled as measured tabular figures.

options.label: Labanotation Score
options.case: Unreadable to bookers; no product carrier.
options.risk: Abstract to the point of confusion.

options.label: Suminagashi Basin
options.case: Pretty but says nothing about restrooms or events.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: Luxury restroom trailer site: dark photo hero, gold accents, amenity icons, gallery, contact form, done impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Night trailer photo full-bleed, headline, Book Now button, three amenity columns below.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other luxury-trailer rental by design.
